The folder in your Nextcloud files. Each song is one ChordPro file in it, named for its title and artist; the setlists are kept beside them in Setlists.json.

Chords, words and tab kept on this phone, to play from without a connection. It goes online to read a song\'s page you send it, keeping the sheet and nothing else, and to sync with your own Nextcloud if you sign in to one.

Your songs stay on this phone. The app collects nothing about you and has no ads or analytics. It goes online only to read a song\'s page whose address you sent it: one page, no pictures or scripts, only over https, saying plainly that it is this app; and, once you sign in to your own Nextcloud, to sync your songs with it. Until then a sheet you type, paste or share here never leaves the phone. The Nextcloud app password is kept on the phone, sealed with a key that cannot leave it; you can revoke it from the server. Files you save go only where you choose to save them.

This app is made by wander wildwood, an independent developer: one person, not a company. That makes wander wildwood the data controller for anything the app itself handles, and that is very little. What you put in stays on this phone unless you send it somewhere yourself. The only things that go out are the app\'s own requests: a request for the one song page whose address you give it, to that site, carrying nothing about you or your songs; and, once you sign in to your own Nextcloud, your songs and their sync requests, to that server alone. Nothing comes to the developer.
Write to email@wanderthe.dev, about your data or anything else.

Under the GDPR you can ask to see the data held about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to limit or object to its use, to take a copy with you, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a data protection authority. Since the app keeps what it stores only on your phone, you can do most of this yourself: delete a song in the app, save every song to a file in Settings, sign out of Nextcloud, clear the app\'s data in Android\'s settings, or uninstall the app. What the sites you ask it to read receive is covered by their own privacy policies. A server of your own is yours: what it keeps is up to you.
